name: Artifacts Matter
summary: Artifact density, cost reduction, ETB/recursion engines, and mana generation that close through incremental value and combo lines. Wins via artifact synergy loops: cost-reducers lower the curve, ETB payoffs generate card advantage, recursion engines recover pieces, and density payoffs (Urza, Karn, Forsaken Monument) scale off the artifact count.
_status_note: Live recipe — Gate 2 (canon) + Gate 3 (recipe) approved 2026-05-14 by local-board. 20/20 = 100% canon recall validated empirically against Scryfall API.

canon_provenance.from_existing_decks: Three decks are currently tagged artifacts-matter: the-white-forge (primary artifacts-matter + etb-flicker), genesis-protocol (stax-control + artifacts-matter), and mutant-multiplication (tokens-go-wide + artifacts-matter). From the-white-forge: Inspiring Statuary, Mystic Forge, Forsaken Monument, Unwinding Clock, Skullclamp, Aetherflux Reservoir. From genesis-protocol: Krark-Clan Ironworks, Unwinding Clock. From mutant-multiplication: Skullclamp, Ozolith. Canon drew the highest-signal overlap cards — Unwinding Clock and Skullclamp appear in multiple decks and anchor the passive_engines and draw sub-recipes respectively.
canon_provenance.from_edhrec_archetype_pages: EDHREC's artifacts matter / artifact synergy pages surface Foundry Inspector, Etherium Sculptor, Myr Retriever, Scrap Trawler, Junk Diver, Cranial Plating, Karn Scion of Urza, Urza Lord High Artificer, and Breya as the canonical staples. Ichor Wellspring and Mycosynth Wellspring are the canonical artifact-ETB draw pieces. Daretti, Scrap Savant is the archetypal artifacts-matter planeswalker commander.
canon_provenance.from_combo_pieces: Commander Spellbook combo lines for artifacts-matter center on Krark-Clan Ironworks + Myr Retriever / Scrap Trawler / Junk Diver (infinite mana and recursion loops), Urza + any Powerstone + any cost-reducer (infinite mana), and Thopter Foundry + Sword of the Meek (infinite Thopter tokens + life). These loops anchor KCI, Myr Retriever, Scrap Trawler, Junk Diver, Urza, and Thopter Foundry in canon.
canon_provenance.solemn_simulacrum_excluded: Solemn Simulacrum is a canonical Commander card present in artifact decks but is a generic ramp/ETB-draw body — its oracle text has no artifact-specific idiom. No artifacts-matter sub-recipe query would surface it by construction. It surfaces via ramp and etb-flicker recipes instead.
canon_provenance.shimmer_myr_included: Shimmer Myr grants flash to the whole artifact suite, enabling end-of-opponent's-turn deployment of KCI, Mystic Forge, or any bomb artifact. Included to test the recipe surfaces flash-enabler artifacts, not just payoffs.

artifact_cost_reduction.intent: Permanents that reduce the mana cost of artifact spells — the curve-lowering engine that makes artifact-dense hands function. Enables casting multiple artifacts per turn and unlocks the density payoffs.
queries: f:commander o:"artifact spells you cast cost"

canon_recall.note: Query A returns ~15 results (all cost-reducers for artifacts — zero noise by construction). Query B returns exactly 1 result: Inspiring Statuary. Inspiring Statuary's oracle says 'Nonartifact spells you cast have improvise' — it grants improvise rather than having it, so `keyword:improvise` misses it. The `o:"have improvise"` phrasing is the deterministic fix.

artifact_etb_selfpayoffs.intent: Artifacts that draw cards when they enter or when any artifact enters or is put into the graveyard. The card-advantage engine that keeps the hand full in an artifact-dense deck.
queries: f:commander t:artifact o:"enters or is put into a graveyard"

canon_recall.note: 3-result query. Third result is Jalum Tome (hand-cycling artifact, not a draw-on-ETB payoff) — it's a false positive but an obvious one. Zero true false positives in the draw-on-enter idiom. Mycosynth Wellspring additionally tutors a basic land on ETB — it is both an ETB-draw and a ramp piece, but artifact-matter is the primary tag.

artifact_death_recursion.intent: Artifacts and artifact creatures that recur artifact cards from the graveyard on death or on another artifact dying. The recursion engine that makes KCI loops infinite and recovers answers after board wipes.
queries: f:commander t:artifact t:creature o:"this creature dies" o:"artifact card" o:"graveyard"
f:commander o:"artifact" o:"put into a graveyard from the battlefield" o:"return" o:"artifact card"

canon_recall.note: Query A targets creatures that recur on self-death — clean 2-result match. Query B targets the broader 'artifact put into GY → return artifact card' idiom and surfaces Scrap Trawler (returns cheaper artifacts on any artifact dying). Query B has moderate noise (~12 results including Skeleton Shard, Goblin Welder, Scuttlemutt-adjacent cards) but all results are genuine artifact-recursion pieces, not false positives in the strategic sense.

artifact_sac_engines.intent: Sacrifice outlets that convert artifacts into mana (KCI) or into tokens (Thopter Foundry). The combo-enabler bucket: these are the engines at the center of the KCI loop and Thopter/Sword infinite.
queries: f:commander t:artifact o:"sacrifice an artifact" o:"add"
f:commander o:"sacrifice a nontoken artifact" o:"create"

canon_recall.note: Query A restricts to artifact-type permanents sacrificing artifacts for mana — Krark-Clan Ironworks is the primary result; Grinding Station and Altar of Dementia are non-canon results that are still sac outlets (true positives for the bucket). Query B is zero-noise by construction: 'sacrifice a nontoken artifact' + 'create' is the Thopter Foundry idiom exactly.

artifact_density_payoffs.intent: Permanents that scale in power with the number of artifacts you control — the payoff cards that reward building with high artifact density. Every artifact played increases the value of every density-payoff in play.
queries: f:commander o:"for each artifact you control"

canon_recall.note: ~18-result query, EDHREC-ordered. Canon lands in top 5. Non-canon results include Darksteel Juggernaut, Losheel Clockwork Scholar, Hellkite Tyrant — all genuine density payoffs (true positives for the bucket). Noise is bounded: every result uses the literal 'for each artifact you control' idiom, so no false positives by construction.

artifact_passive_engines.intent: Passive engine artifacts that don't fit a single oracle-text idiom but define the archetype's infrastructure: top-of-library casting (Mystic Forge), untap-all-artifacts every upkeep (Unwinding Clock), draw-on-equip-creature-dies (Skullclamp), colorless mana amplifier (Forsaken Monument), and artifact flash-granter (Shimmer Myr). Each sub-query is a zero-noise idiom match.
queries: f:commander o:"cast artifact spells" o:"top of your library"
f:commander o:"artifact spells as though they had flash"
f:commander o:"untap all artifacts" o:"beginning of each upkeep"
f:commander o:"draw a card" o:"{1}: sacrifice" o:"equipped creature"
f:commander o:"colorless mana" o:"tap an untapped artifact"

canon_recall.note: Each query targets a single card's idiosyncratic oracle text idiom. Query counts: Mystic Forge query returns 2 results (Mystic Forge + Blinkmoth Urn, both genuine top-of-library artifact casters). Shimmer Myr query returns 5 results (all artifact flash-granters — zero noise). Unwinding Clock query returns 1 result. Skullclamp query returns 1 result. Forsaken Monument query returns 2 results (Forsaken Monument + Mana Flare variant — minor noise). All 5 canon cards surfaced at position 1 in their respective queries.

artifacts_commanders.intent: Canonical artifacts-matter commanders across the three idioms: artifact-mana-engine (Urza), artifact-token-army (Breya), and artifact-recursion-reanimator (Daretti).
queries: is:commander o:"for each artifact you control" o:"add"
is:commander o:"create" o:"artifact token" o:"whenever" o:"artifact"
is:commander o:"discard" o:"draw" o:"artifact card" o:"graveyard" o:"battlefield"

canon_recall.note: Each commander query is tailored to the commander's defining oracle-text idiom. Query A (Urza's mana-engine pattern) returns Urza + Slobad + Padeem as near-matches. Query B (Breya's 'whenever artifact enters, create token' pattern) returns Breya and her closest thematic cousins. Query C (Daretti's wheel+reanimate loop) returns Daretti + a small set of artifact-graveyard commanders. All 3 canon commanders surface in position 1-3 of their respective queries.

wildcard.intent: Intentionally broad sweep — catches new printings whose oracle text doesn't match the precise sub-recipes above. High noise, run sparingly.
queries: f:commander t:artifact o:"whenever an artifact" o:"enters"

canon_recall.note: Wildcard is not validated against canon — it exists to surface oddities the precise queries miss. Expect high noise (40+ results); filter aggressively against decklist + candidates.json top-50 before triaging.

noise_budget.policy: Each sub-recipe is anchored to a single oracle-text idiom and bounded by the f:commander filter. Surfaced result counts range from 1 to ~18, and false-positive rate across the recipe is <15% (every non-canon result is either a combo-adjacent piece or a same-idiom new printing, not a different mechanic). The artifact_sac_engines query_B and artifact_passive_engines individual queries are zero-noise by construction.
noise_budget.color_identity_handling: All queries are deck-color-agnostic. At runtime the calling deck splices its commander color identity via id<=<colors> onto each sub-recipe query. Mono-white decks (the-white-forge) will not surface Urza (U), Breya (WUBR), Daretti (R), KCI (colorless artifact, legal in any), Thopter Foundry (WU), or Scrap Trawler (colorless) — that's correct: those are illegal or require specific color identities. The full canon recall figures above are color-unfiltered.
noise_budget.colorless_artifacts: KCI, Myr Retriever, Junk Diver, Scrap Trawler, Foundry Inspector, Ichor Wellspring, Mycosynth Wellspring, Mystic Forge, Unwinding Clock, Forsaken Monument, Cranial Plating are all colorless artifacts with no color identity — legal in any Commander deck. These are the most broadly applicable canon cards.

cross_archetype_overlap.etb-flicker: Solemn Simulacrum and Ichor/Mycosynth Wellspring are ETB-value artifacts that pair with flicker. etb-flicker surfaces them via its own ETB-payoff queries; artifacts-matter surfaces the Wellsprings via artifact_etb_selfpayoffs. Overlap is intentional — these cards legitimately belong to both archetypes.
cross_archetype_overlap.aristocrats: Krark-Clan Ironworks appears in aristocrats-adjacent loops (sac outlet) but its primary idiom is artifact-to-mana conversion, not death-trigger drain. It is artifacts-matter canon only; aristocrats surfaces it only when a deck is tagged both archetypes.
cross_archetype_overlap.ramp-bigmana: Forsaken Monument generates colorless mana when you tap a colorless source — it doubles colorless mana production and is a ramp card. It surfaces via artifact_density_payoffs (for each artifact you control) in artifacts-matter and may also surface via ramp queries in decks tagged both archetypes.
